project.name: igraph
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source reviewed here is the prepared ARVO container checkout at `c83b6ecdc3fe18dd7fb0cdf0786f43462db2c7d8`; its `src/io/gml.c` line map matches the saved ASan frames at lines 84, 367, and 462, and `src/io/gml.c` itself is unmodified in the working tree. ARVO metadata separately reports `7cd0a0b5ce70bacce2ace8c9f7f3316cbf27484c` as vulnerable and `883bd139af3775d7f90f144c9038a6cb9a28f309` as fixed; both commits exist in the staged history, and the local `patch.diff` matches `883bd139af3775d7f90f144c9038a6cb9a28f309`.

classification.classification_note: The witnessed bug is a stale-pointer dereference in `igraph_read_graph_gml`: a node attribute vector allocated for numeric data is freed during error cleanup, but the caller resumes and reads the freed `igraph_vector_t` header through `VECTOR(*v)` at line 462.

bug_description.original: A use-after-free vulnerability exists in the igraph_read_graph_gml() function.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / exact staged source
bug_description.normalized: The staged `read_gml_fuzzer` harness installs `igraph_error_handler_ignore` and then calls `igraph_read_graph_gml` on the saved `poc`. Inside `igraph_read_graph_gml`, the parsed GML tree contains a node attribute name that is first classified as numeric and later reappears with a tree value under the same name. The first pass leaves `atrec->type` numeric because only string reoccurrences demote a numeric attribute. The second pass therefore takes the numeric node-attribute path, loads `v = (igraph_vector_t *)atrec->value`, and calls `igraph_i_gml_toreal(node, j)` on a tree-typed attribute. The helper's default case executes `IGRAPH_ERROR`, and under `igraph_error_handler_ignore` that runs `IGRAPH_FINALLY_FREE`, which invokes `igraph_i_gml_destroy_attrs` and frees the numeric vector previously stored in `atrec->value`. Because `igraph_i_gml_toreal` returns `igraph_real_t` instead of a status and the caller stores its return value directly, `igraph_read_graph_gml` resumes with stale `v` and line 462 dereferences the freed `igraph_vector_t`, producing the recorded AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ 8.

source.description: First project-code materialization of attacker-controlled input on the crashing path: the staged `poc` is parsed into `context.tree`, which later drives the mixed-type node-attribute state that reaches the use-after-free.
source.value_from: The saved run proves this parse succeeds far enough to reach `igraph_read_graph_gml` line 462. The relevant parsed state is a node attribute name whose first occurrence is integer/real and whose later occurrence under the same name is a nested list/tree.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After error cleanup frees the numeric attribute vector, evaluating `VECTOR(*v)` in this assignment reads the freed `igraph_vector_t` header from stale pointer `v`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 8` at `src/io/gml.c:462:21` in `igraph_read_graph_gml`, on a 24-byte region originally allocated at line 367 and freed through `igraph_i_gml_destroy_attrs` during the helper error path.

root_cause.code: IGRAPH_ERROR("Internal error while parsing GML file", IGRAPH_FAILURE);
root_cause.description: Root cause. The helper signals an error for a non-integer/non-real attribute even though it returns `igraph_real_t`, so under the ignore handler cleanup frees `vattrs` but control still returns to the caller without a checked failure status.
root_cause.note: The fixing patch changes this helper to return `int` and write the numeric result through an output pointer, and both callers at lines 420 and 462 are changed to `IGRAPH_CHECK(igraph_i_gml_toreal(...))` so `igraph_read_graph_gml` exits instead of reusing freed state.

tainted_value_origin.description: The parsed node-attribute value type that seeds the stored attribute classification for an attacker-controlled attribute name.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: For the crashing witness, one node attribute name is first seen with `type` equal to `IGRAPH_I_GML_TREE_INTEGER` or `IGRAPH_I_GML_TREE_REAL`, and a later occurrence of that same name is seen as `IGRAPH_I_GML_TREE_TREE`, which is the only way the later numeric path and helper default case can both execute.

parser_admitted.description: The saved run reaches the post-parse loops and crashes much later at line 462, so `igraph_gml_yyparse` must have accepted enough of the malformed GML input to materialize `context.tree` and enter the node-attribute passes.

harness_context.description: The fuzz harness installs the ignore handler, so later `IGRAPH_ERROR` calls execute `IGRAPH_FINALLY_FREE()` and return to the caller instead of aborting immediately.

coarse_trace.summary: The GML parser materializes `context.tree`, and the first node-attribute scan records an attacker-controlled attribute name as numeric.

A later occurrence of the same attribute name has tree type but does not demote `atrec->type`, so `igraph_read_graph_gml` allocates numeric storage for that attribute and later selects the numeric node-attribute write path.

The numeric conversion helper rejects the tree-typed value, and under `igraph_error_handler_ignore` the finally-stack cleanup frees the numeric attribute vector while the helper still returns to its caller.
Back at line 462, the caller resumes with stale `v` and dereferences the freed `igraph_vector_t`, producing the observed heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.note: Source. `igraph_gml_yyparse` consumes the staged `poc` and materializes `context.tree`. The saved run later reaches line 462 in the same function, so this parse succeeded far enough to create the node/attribute structure that drives the mixed-type attribute path.

During the first node-attribute census, the first occurrence of an attacker-controlled attribute name is seen with integer/real type, so the shared `igraph_attribute_record_t` for that name is created in `vattrs` and classified as `IGRAPH_ATTRIBUTE_NUMERIC`.

A later occurrence of that same attribute name is tree-typed, but this update logic only demotes a numeric attribute when the later value is a string. For a tree value, `atrec->type` stays numeric, preserving the wrong interpretation into the later fill pass.

Because the stored classification is still numeric, the later allocation pass creates an `igraph_vector_t` for this attribute and saves its heap pointer in `atrec->value`. This is the 24-byte object ASan reports as allocated at line 367. The surrounding `igraph_read_graph_gml` frame had already registered `igraph_i_gml_destroy_attrs` on the finally stack at line 220, so this vector becomes part of error cleanup ownership.

In the node-attribute fill pass, the later tree-typed occurrence resolves through `vattrnames` to the same shared `atrec`. Because step 3 left `atrec->type` numeric, this branch is taken and `v` aliases the heap vector from step 4.

fine_trace.code: IGRAPH_ERROR("Internal error while parsing GML file", IGRAPH_FAILURE);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The later occurrence's actual tree type reaches `igraph_i_gml_toreal`, which enters the default case. Under the harness's `igraph_error_handler_ignore`, this error path runs `IGRAPH_FINALLY_FREE()`, which invokes `igraph_i_gml_destroy_attrs` and frees the numeric vector from step 4 together with its containing attribute records. But `igraph_i_gml_toreal` still returns from an `igraph_real_t` function, so the failure is not propagated as a checked status and the caller resumes with stale `v`.

Sink. After step 6 returns, this same assignment resumes in the caller. Evaluating `VECTOR(*v)` dereferences the freed `igraph_vector_t` that `v` still points to, causing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ 8 at `src/io/gml.c:462:21`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: No. ASan's allocation context is the numeric attribute vector allocated at `gml.c:367`; the project bug is the later error-propagation failure at `gml.c:84` and the unchecked caller state at `gml.c:462` that reuses that freed vector.

format.name: GML
format.contract: A malformed GML graph that still parses into `context.tree` and includes a node attribute name whose first occurrence is integer/real and whose later occurrence under the same name is a nested list/tree, so `igraph_read_graph_gml` keeps the attribute classified numeric but later calls `igraph_i_gml_toreal` on a tree-typed node attribute.
